design_goal: Make role assignment feel like a one-second decision during onboarding, and make role enforcement feel invisible during normal work — surfacing only when a scoped user needs to understand or escalate their access.
constraints: Only Full Access admins can assign or change roles
Role enforcement at both UI and API layers — no client-only gating
Last Full Access admin cannot downgrade their own role
Four fixed roles — no custom role builder in v1
Bulk role operations out of scope for v1
SCIM/IdP provisioning out of scope for v1
Dashboard Viewer scope (cross-surface vs. scoped) unresolved — strategy assumes cross-surface read-only pending PM confirmation
selected_strategy_rationale: User-first assignment pattern (inline badge click → popover → confirmation modal) is simpler than role-first flows and matches Adaptive Security's observed best practice. First-login awareness banner addresses the most critical anti-pattern in the category — scoped users with no awareness of their permission boundary. Permission-denied state with 'Request access' CTA closes the escalation dead end no competitor currently solves.

alternative_strategies.name: Dedicated Role Management Screen
alternative_strategies.summary: Standalone settings screen where admins configure role definitions and assign users by role
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Adds unnecessary abstraction for four fixed roles. Splits user and role management into separate contexts. Only justified when the role model becomes customizable — not for v1.

alternative_strategies.name: Role Assignment in User Detail Drawer
alternative_strategies.summary: Clicking a user row opens a right-anchored drawer with full user details including role selector
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Too heavyweight as the primary invite-time assignment path. Appropriate as an edit sub-flow for existing users but not the default. The inline table approach is faster for bulk invites.

tradeoffs: Hidden navigation (vs. disabled with tooltip) means new scoped users have no passive awareness of gated surfaces — first-login banner partially mitigates this but is dismissible
Dashboard Viewer as cross-surface read-only creates a data inversion vs. functional managers — requires PM confirmation before design begins
No SCIM in v1 is an enterprise objection risk — requires explicit 'Directory sync coming soon' messaging in the product
'Request access' CTA requires either an in-app notification center or a mailto: fallback — decision blocks escalation screen design
assumptions: Dashboard Viewer is cross-surface read-only (org-wide data visibility) — pending PM confirmation
Dashboard is a single component with role-filtered data at the API layer, not separate UI surfaces per role
Audit log lives as a sub-tab in User Management, not a standalone surface
First-login banner is sufficient awareness for scoped users — no blocking modal required
Export is available to Dashboard Viewers as a read-only action
